skill.name: perigon-backend
skill.description: Guides backend work in Perigon ASP.NET Core projects using EF Core, Modules, Services, managers, controllers, and Aspire AppHost conventions.
skill.summary: Apply Perigon backend conventions for ASP.NET Core, EF Core, and Aspire projects.
skill.author: AterDev

security_audit.summary: All five static system reconnaissance findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and adjudicated as false positives. The skill contains backend architecture guidance only, with no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unauthorized system inspection instructions found.

static_findings.snippet: - Entities: inherit EntityBase (Id, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, IsDeleted); Id uses Guid v7 client-generat
- Database: favor SQL Server (commercial) or PostgreSQL; use foreign keys within a domain; avoid str
- Managers: place in src/Modules/{Mod}/Managers; inherit ManagerBase (generic when tied to entity) f
- Controllers: under src/Services/*/Controllers; inherit RestControllerBase. Use HTTP verb attribute
- Aspire/AppHost: AppHost orchestrates infra/services; ensure Docker/Podman running. Configure via a

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 10 describes entity modeling rules for IDs, timestamps, strings, decimals, enums, and date types. It does not request host discovery, credential access, or environment reconnaissance.
Line 11 describes database selection, relational modeling, and migration file locations. The reference to a migration script is project guidance, not an instruction to inspect the system.
Line 13 describes where managers belong and which base operations they should use. It does not instruct the agent to enumerate files, processes, users, or system configuration.
Line 15 gives controller layering and HTTP response conventions. The mention of auth, permissions, and validation is ordinary application design guidance.
Line 16 mentions Docker, Podman, appsettings, and editor diagnostics as development prerequisites. It also tells the agent to avoid build or run commands unless requested.

content.value_statement: Perigon backend work requires strict architecture, EF Core, and Aspire conventions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through those project patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guides entity design using EntityBase, Guid v7 IDs, timestamps, soft deletes, and typed date fields.
Defines EF Core conventions for DbContext placement, migrations, projections, tracking, and bulk operations.
Explains manager placement, ManagerBase inheritance, dependency injection, transactions, and business exception handling.
Specifies DTO folder structure and expected Detail, Add, Update, Item, and Filter model shapes.
Describes controller placement, RestControllerBase usage, HTTP verb methods, responses, and validation boundaries.
Summarizes Aspire AppHost configuration through appsettings files and local container prerequisites.
limitations: It provides conventions only and does not include executable code or scaffolding scripts.
It assumes an existing Perigon repository with the described src folder layout.
It does not validate database schemas, migrations, or controller behavior by itself.
It avoids build and run commands unless the user explicitly requests them.

best_practices: Keep business rules in managers and keep HTTP concerns in controllers.
Use typed DTO shapes for detail, add, update, item, and filter workflows.
Prefer projected no-tracking queries unless updates or tracking are required.
anti_patterns: Do not return ActionResult from managers or access HttpContext inside managers.
Do not store related values as string-delimited lists when relationships, arrays, or JSON fit better.
Do not wrap every API response in a custom ApiResponse when standard responses are expected.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Perigon backend projects using ASP.NET Core, EF Core, Modules, Services, and Aspire AppHost conventions.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations?
faq.answer: No. It explains where migrations belong and references project conventions, but it does not run commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it help design new entities?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply rules for EntityBase, Guid v7 IDs, string lengths, decimal precision, enums, and date types.

faq.question: Can it review controller code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check inheritance, HTTP verb attributes, method names, response types, validation, and manager boundaries.

faq.question: Does it replace project tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides architectural guidance and review support, but tests and diagnostics still need to be run separately.
